A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIST research. All pages, equations, tables, figures, and references support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-modeling, in-context learning, open-domain QA, ablation, and semantic-distance experiments, including TinyLlama and Mistral implementations.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds long-context baseline comparisons, throughput measurements, and revised masking-ablation results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same context split, frozen ViT-L/14, trainable Perceiver Resampler, cross-attention integration, contrastive PVE objective, and 50% frequency-based masking. The slow-fast terminology reframes the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same RedPajama training corpus, five language-modeling datasets, eleven ICL datasets, and three QA datasets. Proof and Code rename ProofPile and CodeParrot. The masking ablation switches between already-covered datasets; the new multilingual discussion does not document additional evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: V3 Table 1 adds Replug, Stream, and adapted ToMe and FastV comparisons to the existing TinyLlama/CEPE comparison. This substantially broadens comparison methods to alternative long-context processing and visual compression approaches. ICL and QA comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 introduces throughput relative to TinyLlama and removes the 2048-total-token evaluation setting. New ToMe/FastV comparisons match VIST's compression ratio and retain its Resampler and PVE. Training data preparation, retained context lengths, ICL sampling, demonstration allocation, and QA retrieval procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The masking-strategy ablation changes its ICL columns from SST5/MR in v1 Table 4 to NLUS/NLUI in v3 Table 5. Token-count, training-length, Mistral, and semantic-distance analyses are retained. Reordered figures preserve the same plotted curves.

E5.justification: Both versions report ICL accuracy averaged over three seeds, explicitly 42, 43, and 44. Neither introduces confidence intervals, standard deviations, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V3 substantially expands Table 1 with four baselines' perplexity/resource results and throughput measurements, including 7.6× for VIST versus 3.3× for CEPE at 16k context, relative to TinyLlama. It removes the 2k-context rows and replaces masking-ablation classification results. Retained VIST/CEPE benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) retain the same contrastive loss, Shannon information formula, and token-importance definition. Adding the PVE loss subscript and human-reading motivation does not introduce new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central vision-compression and efficiency claims persist. V3 presents VIST as a human-inspired slow-fast framework and changes the abstract's claimed average advantage from 5.7% to 7.6%, naming different benchmark examples. The introduction also adds explicit tokenizer and multilingual-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V3 adds human-skimming interpretations, explanations for classification gaps and ToMe/FastV weaknesses, and an explicit English-focus qualification. Its new claim that CEPE degrades with more encoded QA passages conflicts with Table 3, where all three CEPE scores increase from 5 to 20 passages.

D1.justification: V3 documents the ToMe/FastV adaptations and mentions precomputed token-frequency statistics. It omits v1's CEPE 256-token chunking detail and 1.28-patches-per-token estimate. A new promise to release source code supplies no access link; most existing implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 substantially reframes its motivation through newly cited eye-movement, skimming, and word-skipping research. It also expands positioning around additional long-context and visual-compression methods. CEPE remains the closest prior work, but the contrast increasingly emphasizes semantic redundancy and attention allocation.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around human reading, and related work is condensed. The Mistral extension moves into the ablation section, token-redundancy visualization moves into Discussion, and the Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Figure 1 is completely redrawn; tables are resized and restructured, including throughput and demonstration-allocation columns. Ablation tables and semantic-distance figures are reordered, with revised captions and labels.

improvement.justification: The additional relevant baselines and throughput results in Table 1 address v1's narrow comparative evidence, providing a modest net improvement in empirical support. The gains are limited by unchanged core results, omitted implementation details, and the new unsupported claim that CEPE worsens with additional QA passages despite Table 3 showing increases.
